description: A FUNCTION-ID paragraph opening a user-defined function definition (ISO §2023:11.5 Format 1 / §2023:10.6.1 function-definition) and its END FUNCTION marker (§2023:10.7.2) - COBOL-2002 introductions (kb/Work PB988, row FMT-10.7.2). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 Identification Division opens with 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. program-name.' (§1985:VI.3.2.1.1) and its one end marker is 'END PROGRAM program-name.' (§1985:X.2.5.2), so X3.23-1985 has neither the paragraph nor the end-marker alternative; the 2002 compilation group adds the function-definition, opened by 'FUNCTION-ID. user-function-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ].' and closed by 'END FUNCTION user-function-name-1.' (§2002:10.5.1), §2002:F.1 item 6 lists FUNCTION-ID under 'Reserved words. The following reserved words have been added', and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 142: 'User-defined functions. The ability was added to write functions that are activated in a manner similar to intrinsic functions.' 2014 and 2023 keep both (§2014:10.6.1, §2023:10.6.1: 'END FUNCTION user-function-name-1.'; §2014:11.5, §2023:11.5.1: 'The FUNCTION-ID paragraph specifies the name by which a function is identified'). Below 2002 VersionConformancePass ParseArm.VisitFunctionIdParagraph names the edition (0900) on recognition. The prototype format (IS PROTOTYPE) is its own row, function-prototype-2002, fired on the prototypePhrase node, so a prototype is gated once. END FUNCTION closing a PROGRAM-ID unit is §2023:10.6.1's keyword rule (COBOL2274) at every edition, so no END FUNCTION reaches an accepted COBOL-85 source.
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
FUNCTION-ID. FDDBL.
DATA DIVISION.
LINKAGE SECTION.
01 L-X PIC 9(4).
01 L-R PIC 9(4).
PROCEDURE DIVISION USING L-X RETURNING L-R.
P.
    COMPUTE L-R = L-X * 2.
    GOBACK.
END FUNCTION FDDBL.
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMFD1.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
CONFIGURATION SECTION.
REPOSITORY.
    FUNCTION FDDBL.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 W PIC 9(4).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    COMPUTE W = FUNCTION FDDBL(21).
    STOP RUN.
END PROGRAM VMFD1.
